feed.title: The SpaceX Dispatch
feed.subtitle: Weekday briefing on SpaceX launches, Starlink, AI and the SPCX stock
feed.rights: The SpaceX Dispatch is an independent weekday digest of public news, X posts, regulatory filings and market data about Space Exploration Technologies Corp., and is not affiliated with the company. Quotes are verbatim; emoji in quoted posts are omitted for print. Market data are delayed and may be revised. Not investment advice.

entry.title: Monday, October 12, 2026: The SDA satellites fly, and Musk puts a ship catch on Starship's next flight
entry.summary:
A Falcon 9 finally launched 21 Space Development Agency (SDA) data-relay satellites from California early Saturday, five days after an automatic abort, and its booster landed back at Vandenberg. Two more Falcon 9s are lined up: Starlink 15-25 on Monday evening, after slipping from Saturday and Sunday, and the CRS-35 cargo Dragon to the International Space Station (ISS) at 6:33 a.m. EDT Tuesday.

Speaking by video at a Tesla fan event in Texas on Saturday, Elon Musk said Starship Flight 15, "hopefully" four to six weeks away, will try to catch the ship with the launch tower. Starlink won a full operating license in Venezuela and offered free service in quake-hit Panama, while Musk escalated his fight with Mukesh Ambani over India. SPCX rose 1.25% Friday to $162.57 as Barclays started coverage at Overweight. SpaceX has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Friday morning.

entry.title: Friday, October 9, 2026: SpaceX buys its way into the phone business, and carrier stocks take the hit
entry.summary:
After the market closed on Thursday, SpaceX said it will buy Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio, up to 14 megahertz of paired low-band airwaves that it says will let Starlink Mobile "become a major mobile carrier in the US." The price was not disclosed; The Wall Street Journal reported about $8 billion in cash. The deal still needs approval from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). By Friday morning, shares of AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile were down 5.5% to 7.4% before the open, Reuters reported.

The news came too late to help SPCX, which fell 4.19% to $160.57 during Thursday's session, its second straight loss, before rising about 2.5% in extended trading. Up to 328.4 million more Class A shares become free to sell from Friday under the IPO lock-up schedule. Crew-12 is home after Thursday's splashdown. Next on the launch schedule: a Space Development Agency (SDA) mission early Saturday and the CRS-35 cargo flight on Tuesday. SpaceX has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Thursday morning.

entry.title: Thursday, October 8, 2026: Crew-12 splashes down, Starlink signs up whole airlines, and Elon Musk takes his India fight public
entry.summary:
The Dragon capsule Freedom splashed down off Los Angeles at 11:34 a.m. EDT Thursday, bringing four Crew-12 astronauts home after 237 days at the International Space Station (ISS). Starlink had a strong day with airlines: American Airlines will put it on its entire mainline fleet of more than 1,000 jets, KLM will offer it free on long-haul flights from mid-2027, and Royal Air Maroc became the first African airline to sign on.

In India, Elon Musk accused "certain oligarchs" of blocking Starlink's license, and the government called the claim baseless. On Wall Street, a report that SpaceX is seeking about $40 billion of debt to buy Nvidia chips helped push SPCX down 2.51% to $167.60 on Wednesday, ending a three-day run. In Washington, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) put two direct-to-device spectrum proposals on its October 29 agenda. SpaceX has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Wednesday morning.
